title: Aggregation query rewriter for tenant-aware metric masking in analytics pipeline
creator: Aditi Shah
description:
Summary: Implement a query rewrite layer in the analytics aggregation service that enforces tenant- and role-aware masking at aggregation time instead of relying solely on expensive row-level filters. Goal is to reduce query latency and memory pressure for high-cardinality usage views while preserving strict permission boundaries for sensitive metrics and dimensions.

Motivation and scope:
- Current approach applies row-level RBAC filters as a pre-query step which results in large scans and memory blowups for cross-tenant rollups and high-cardinality joins (seen in incidents #INC-2025-09 and monthly spikes on dashboard `analytics/query-latency`).
- For many common console views (per-tenant summary, per-route token counts, daily token rollups) we can compute masked aggregates using a rewrite that replaces sensitive dimension groups with precomputed "masked buckets" or uses aggregation-time filters derived from entitlement projections.
- This ticket covers design + implementation of the rewrite middleware inside the aggregation API, integration with the entitlement projection service, unit + integration tests, and a staged canary rollout on dedicated analytics hosts.

Design decisions and trade-offs considered:
- Pushdown vs. Post-aggregation masking: pushing masks into the aggregation stage reduces data scanned but requires stronger guarantees from materialized views. We will prefer pushdown for stable aggregates and fall back to post-aggregation masking for ad-hoc queries.
- Deterministic masked buckets: to keep counts comparable across tenants and avoid leaking cardinality, we will map sensitive dimension values to a small set of deterministic masked labels per-tenant-authorization-scope. This sacrifices granularity but preserves safety and aggregation semantics.
- Cache invalidation: aggregates backed by masked buckets need cache keys that include the authorization fingerprint (entitlement version). We will bump materialized aggregate versions on entitlement schema changes — trade-off is more cache churn.
- Performance vs. precision: for P0 latency SLO routes we will prefer approximate masked aggregates (precomputed) to meet 99th percentile latency; for exploratory queries we will allow more expensive row-level enforcement.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Design rewrite DSL and mapping rules (contrib: design doc at Confluence).
2) Implement entitlement fingerprint header propagation from Console -> Query Gateway -> Aggregation API.
3) Rewrite layer: accept logical aggregation AST, transform sensitive group-by columns into masked expressions or join to masked_buckets table.
4) Materialized aggregate versioning + cache key change using entitlement fingerprint.
5) Tests: unit tests for rewrite rules, golden testcases for representative queries, integration tests with entitlement projection service and the tenant simulator.
6) Deployment: staged canary on analytics-dedicated hosts (20% traffic), monitor latency & accuracy signals, then roll to 100%.

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ANALYTICS/Aggregation+Query+Rewriter
- RFC: https://docs.redwood.ai/rfcs/2026-aggregation-query-rewriter.md
- Github PR (draft): https://github.com/redwood-inference/console-analytics/pull/3982
- Dashboard for rollout: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/analytics-query-rewrite/rollout
- Incident context: https://incidents.redwood.ai/INC-2025-09

Acceptance criteria:
- Aggregation API exposes rewrite layer flag `X-Auth-Fingerprint` and uses it in cache keys (verified via unit tests).
- Representative dashboard queries show >=30% reduction in p95 latency in canary for masked-eligible routes compared to baseline.
- No cross-tenant leakage in synthetic test harness (private test with 1000 simulated tenants).
- Automated integration tests cover at least 12 golden query patterns and run in CI.

Open questions / blockers:
- Finalize the masked_buckets schema and retention (security review blocking until schema is approved).
- Entitlement fingerprint TTL: how often should the projection service emit new versions? Current proposal is hourly; ops prefers daily to reduce churn.
- Backwards compatibility: how to handle older console versions that don't send fingerprint header? Plan: default to conservative row-level enforcement for missing header.

Next steps and timeline:
- 2026-02-20: complete DSL design and get security review (owner: Aditi Shah).
- 2026-02-26: merge entitlement-propagation PR and feature flag behind `agg-rewriter`.
- 2026-03-01: deploy canary to analytics-dedicated-1 (20% traffic).
- 2026-03-15: evaluate metrics and expand rollout if stable.
